articles.title: Scorching Heat Dome Tests World Cup: How FIFA and Host Cities Are Responding
articles.summary: A record-breaking heat wave is slamming North American World Cup host cities, with feels-like temps up to 110°F. Toronto’s open-air stadium exposes 43,000 fans; Kansas City faces an extreme heat warning. FIFA’s hydration breaks spark controversy.

articles.title: When Nights Don't Cool Down: The Hidden Danger of the Current Heat Wave
articles.summary: A heat dome is pushing daytime temps past 100°F across the U.S., but overnight lows are staying shockingly high—in the 80s. This prevents body recovery and raises heat illness risk, especially for the 12% of households without AC. Climate change is driving the trend.

articles.title: Kane’s Late Brace Saves England from Humiliation, But Tuchel’s Problems Mount
articles.summary: England narrowly avoided a catastrophic World Cup exit, beating DR Congo 2-1 on Harry Kane’s late double. The win masks deep flaws: an unsettled defense, a right-back crisis, and over-reliance on Kane and Bellingham. Next: a daunting clash with Mexico at Azteca Stadium.
